items.title: Second case against Catholic priest Cyprian Pinto for alleged sexual assault of teen boy
items.summary: A second case has been registered against Father Cyprian Pinto, the parish priest of St Vincent Ferrer Church in Valencia, Mangaluru, over allegations of sexually assaulting a 13-year-old boy, the Mangaluru City Police said on November 9. According to a press release issued by the Mangaluru City Police, the Mangaluru Women Police Station registered the case based on a complaint alleging that Pinto (65) sexually assaulted the boy on May 13, 2026. The boy regularly attended Sunday prayers at St Sebastian Church in Permannur village. The investigation into the second case has been handed over to the Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP), Central Sub-Division, Mangaluru City. Pinto was earlier booked by the Mangaluru South Police Station on October 15 following a complaint alleging sexual harassment of a 14-year-old boy. He was arrested on October 17 and produced before a court on October 18. He was remanded to judicial custody until October 30 and subsequently released on bail. The Additional District and Sessions Judge of the Fast Track Special Court-I in Mangaluru granted Pinto bail on October 29. Judge KS Manu imposed conditions requiring him to cooperate with the investigation and refrain from tampering with evidence or intimidating witnesses. The allegations against Pinto first came to light after five boys and their parents reportedly approached Mangalore Bishop Peter Paul Saldanha on August 17. The children had each written letters detailing the alleged abuse. The bishop had been informed about the allegations nearly two months before the police registered an FIR. The bishop had reportedly ordered an internal inquiry conducted by the diocesan Judicial Vicar Naveen Pinto and another priest, Melwyn Peres. A community member previously told TNM that the inquiry lasted around two weeks, with the children and their parents being summoned individually or in small groups. The inquiry report was reportedly sent to the Vatican, although TNM could not independently confirm this. The Karnataka Directorate of Child Protection had also written to the Dakshina Kannada District Child Protection Unit (DCPU) on August 31, directing it to enquire into the allegations. The DCPU subsequently wrote to the Mangaluru South police on September 2, seeking an investigation. The October 15 FIR followed a complaint by one of the boys. items.title: Video of TN Deputy Speaker slapping man goes viral, victim coerced to deny incident?
items.summary: Edit: Karthik has now changed his statement, alleging that he was threatened into making the video absolving the legislator of wrongdoing. Deputy Speaker Ravi Shankar allegedly threatened to kill his family if he did not record the statement. Karthik has also accused a police officer of intimidating him and forcing him to make the video at the legislator’s residence. Hours after a video showing Tamil Nadu Deputy Speaker and Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) MLA Ravi Shankar assaulting a man went viral, the victim released another video alongside the legislator, claiming that the incident was being “wrongly” portrayed on social media. The man, identified as Karthik Kumar, a resident of Tiruchirappalli district, had reportedly approached the MLA with complaints about drinking water shortages and garbage accumulation in his neighbourhood. In the video of the alleged assault, the MLA is heard asking Kumar, “Which village are you from?” before repeatedly slapping him, despite Karthik saying, “I have voted for Vijay. I have voted for Thalapathy”. The incident took place on Sunday, November 9, during the Deepavali festival. Following the alleged assault, Karthik was admitted to the Manachanallur Government Hospital for treatment. After the assault video went viral, another video was released in which Karthik is seen sitting next to Ravi Shankar and saying that nothing serious had happened. He claimed there was some pushing and shoving because of the crowd and that the incident was being portrayed wrongly. “I came to meet the Deputy Speaker at his residence. Because of the crowd, there was some pushing and shoving. Nothing else happened. Some people are sharing the video on social media and projecting it wrongly. We belong to the same party and are like a family. Do not believe the rumours of those saying otherwise,” Kumar said. Ravi Shankar is seen nodding as Karthik makes the statement. The man who was allegedly assaulted by Tamil Nadu Deputy Speaker and TVK MLA Ravi Shankar has now alleged that he was threatened into making a subsequent video statement absolving the legislator of wrongdoing. Karthik Kumar, who had earlier appeared in a video alongside Ravi Shankar saying that nothing had happened, claims that the MLA threatened to kill his family if he did not record the statement. He has also accused the police of intimidating him and forcing him to make the video at the legislator’s residence.
